 Dated this the 27th day of November, 2025
 J U D G M E N T
Sathish Ninan, J.
The original petition filed by the husband against the wife seeking dissolution of marriage, was dismissed by the Family Court.
The husband is in appeal.
2. The marriage between the parties was solemnised on 06.11.2003.
According to the husband he is a member of a joint family consisting of his mother, sister and family, brother and family, and his uncle and aunt.
This was informed to the wife and family prior to the marriage.
After the marriage the wife insisted that they should start separate residence.
It was not acceded to by the husband.
Thereafter he was being mentally tortured.
Since 18.05.2008 the wife is residing at a parental house after a visit at a temple festival near to her parental residence.
Though in an attempt to ease out the differences he 2025:KER:91334 approached the District Legal Services Authority, it ended in futility.
He seeks for dissolution of marriage.
3. The wife denied the allegations of desertion and cruelty.
She contended that she was being treated cruelly at the matrimonial house and that she was being looked upon as a mere maid servant.
She alleges that she was driven out of the matrimonial home on 18.05.2008 when she insisted to attend the festival at the temple near her parental house.
The Family Court held that the evidence on record is insufficient to grant a decree.
4. We have heard the learned counsel on either side.

5. It is the definite allegation of the husband that, prior to the marriage the wife and the family were informed that the husband's family is a joint family consisting of the families of his brother and sister and also his mother.

Though the wife, in the objections filed to the original petition, did not deny the same in its entirety, she added that she was assured that his brother and family will shift to another house which is under construction.
Regarding the sister, the wife was informed that they would start separate residence by renting out a house.
She 2025:KER:91334 was told that only the husband's mother, uncle and aunt would be there at the residence.

Paragraph 4 of the objection Gopalakrishna Kammath vs Sreejyothi on 27 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196060339/
2 reads thus :-
"4

,           
    
  
   

  

  

   
 
   

 

   
     
   
 
   

 
    

 
 


 
   
 


,  

 


  
 


 
  
 


 

    
    
 


 
    
 

  
, 
  
 
  
  
       

       
   
, 
  
 
       
 
   
, 
     
   
   
  
  
 
   
 
       
 
   
  



 
        
   

 

  
       
 
 
    
  
  

          
 
  
 
      
  
      
   


.   
  

 
  
 

 



  -    


, 

 
 

     


. "
Therefore, it is evident that the wife was aware that the husband's family was living as a joint family along with his mother, brother
, sister, uncle and aunt

. But for the ipse dixit of the wife, there is no evidence to find that there was an understanding that the husband's brother and sister would start separate residence or that the construction of any other house was in progress.
Even when the wife was examined, it was her 2025:KER:91334 definite stand that she is willing to resume cohabitation provided that the petitioner starts separate residence.
Therefore it is evident that the husband's allegation that the wife was harassing him seeking separate residence is quite probable.

When the wife and family were well informed about the circumstances in which her husband and family were residing, the insistence of the wife for separate residence leaving the other members of his family,
especially his aged mother, would certainly amount to infliction of mental cruelty.
6. So also, it has come out that the wife had filed a criminal case against the husband under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code.
The case ended in acquittal.
Filing false criminal complaints and harassing the husband would also amount to mental cruelty.
7. Admittedly the parties having been living separately since 18.05.2008 and 17 years have elapsed since then.
We find that the husband is entitled for a decree for dissolution of 2025:KER:91334 marriage.
Resultantly, this appeal is allowed.
The marriage between the parties will stand dissolved by a decree of divorce.

Sd/-
